answer: Ridge-Priced Admission Curve: identities draw shared capacity from a rising marginal cost curve, so each new registration in a window costs more than the last. Enforcement: total admitted identities per window is capped by where marginal cost crosses expected attacker value, and the curve's ridge steepens with burst rate. An attacker flooding registrations pays geometrically escalating fees, while slow organic growth stays on the cheap karst-like floor. Honest latecomers wait one window; a dune of fresh identities collapses under its own price.
